В нея, за постигането на просветление са необходими единствено самоанализ и вътрешно изследване.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"OQSAbaJ5XS","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"8yfkg05yt0e","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"„Наставления за практичен начин на живот и други неоконфуциански съчинения\" (傳習錄), Уан Янмин","text":"„Нищо не съществува извън нашите умове, нито един висш принцип не съществува извън нашите сърца.“","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"DdDr7Iwt-Q","type":"media","data":{"id":"n3uyi06ev","poster":{},"items":[{"image":{"id":1229,"preview":"https://assets.wemeditate.com/uploads/media_file/file/1229/small_002d22d4ff.jpg?version="},"alt":"Handwriting of Wang Yangming","caption":"Writings of Wang Yangming, an influential figure in Confucian meditation ","credit":""}],"mediaFiles":[1229],"youtube_id":"","type":"image","quantity":"single","position":"center","size":"wide","decorations":{}}},{"id":"eVYMMkj2-4","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"zaosj9gsoor","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"превод Дейвид Хинтън","credit":"„Джуандзъ”, глава 4","text":"Конфуций отговаря: „Толкова много постановления! Издавате закони, но не обмисляте нещата докрай. Да, вярно е, че ще спрете гнева му. Но това е всичко, което бихте спрели. Как ще го накарате да се промени? Все още превръщате ума в учител.“
„Тогава нямам никаква идея\", добави Йен Хуей накрая. „Мога ли да попитам каква би била вашата стратегия?“„Пост” - отвърна Конфуций. „Нека ви обясня нещо. Да използвате ума си, за да вършите неща – това не е ли твърде лесно? А лесният начин рядко се съгласува със светлото небе.“
„Къщата ми е скромна“, рече Йен Хуей. „От месеци не съм вкусвал вино или месо. Не се ли смята това за пост?“
„Това е постът на церемонията и ритуала\", отговорил Конфуций. „Не е постът на ума.\"„Мога ли да попитам за поста на ума?\"„Съсредоточете вашето внимание.“ - започна Конфуций. „Спрете да слушате с ушите си и слушайте с ума си. След това спрете да слушате с ума си и слушайте с вашия първичен дух. Слушането е ограничено до ухото. Умът се ограничава до пресмятане на нещата. Но първичният дух е празен: той е просто това, което очаква нещата. Пътят е слята празнота, а празнотата е постът на ума.\"

Малко медитативни практики са оцелели в организираната европейска религия и затова голяма част от обновяването на западната медитация е подхранвано от изучаването на източните практики, както и от миграцията на източни мистици на запад, особено от Индия и Китай.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"WCMurJ1SrN","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"5poh9pmg08i","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"„Уолдън“, 1854 г., Хенри Дейвид Торо","text":"„Сутрин къпя интелекта си в грандиозната и космогонична философия на \"Бхагават гита\", от чието написване са изминали години на боговете и в сравнение с която нашият съвременен свят и неговата литература изглеждат нищожни и тривиални; и се съмнявам дали тази философия не трябва да се отнесе към предишно състояние на съществуване, толкова далечна е нейната възвишеност от нашите представи.\"","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"zKh3Ik48Pn","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"5xn4oy22x1s","text":"Източният и западният свят не са се развивали изолирани един от друг. Европейците са изучавали източната култура още в древна Гърция - там, където в източните части на империята на Александър Велики са се формирали гръко-будистки общества. През второто хилядолетие европейските учени били шокирани да открият силното сходство между латинския и санскрит (корените на езиците съответно на Европа и Индия). Великите мислители трансценденталисти от ранната американска култура - Ралф Уолдо Емерсън, Хенри Дейвид Торо и други, се задълбочават в изучаването на индийските свещени текстове.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"h-7jwTKbUn","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"54u9db7kcuq","text":"Източните влияния вече са виртуално неотделими от западната медитация. В средата и края на ХХ в. американското контракултурно движение и миграцията на религиозни дейци от комунизма в Източна Азия, предизвикват експлозия на интереса към източните медитативни практики на запад. Западната медитация има много ясни връзки с източните практики, но също така се е развила, за да включи западните възгледи. Карл Юнг - влиятелен психолог от XX в., предлага своята философия на медитацията, която е добър пример за философия, черпеща от източното влияние и адаптирана на Запад.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"xGJaM0QU_C","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"9ecgdp2qb5","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"„The Conjunction“, CW 14, par. 709., Карл Юнг","text":"„Като цяло медитацията и съзерцанието имат лоша репутация на Запад. Те се разглеждат като особено осъдителна форма на безделие или като патологичен нарцисизъм. Никой няма време за себепознание или не вярва, че то може да послужи за някаква разумна цел. Освен това човек предварително знае, че не си струва труда да познава себе си, защото всеки глупак може да разбере какво представлява. Ние вярваме изключително в правенето и не питаме този, който прави, който се оценява само по постиженията, които имат колективна стойност. Изглежда, че широката общественост е осъзнала съществуването на несъзнаваната психика повече от така наречените експерти, но все още никой не е направил изводи от факта, че западният човек се сблъсква със себе си като с чужденец и че самопознанието е едно от най-трудните и взискателни изкуства.“","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"Bh8BkPI9IZ","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"z821j3hbrq","text":"Карл Юнг оприличава медитацията като „примиряване с несъзнаваното“. Тя е инструмент за истинско самопознание и в този смисъл той я дистанцира от религиозните медитативни практики, които по негово време често са се превръщали в ритуални или гледащи навън.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"-zUWREnEkI","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"dr98xwooosb","text":"И така, от къде произлиза медитацията?","type":"header","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"rshqAkUiZ3","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"7dsr0k2ildp","text":"Най-добре проследената линия на медитацията произхожда от Индия, а след това се разпространява на изток в Китай с будизма - по-специално в дзен-будистката традиция. Гръцки учени и американски трансценденталисти са изучавали тази линия. Тя оказва влияние върху суфизма по време на ислямското владичество в Индия. Най-разпространените съвременни практики имат дълбоки корени в тази линия и затова Индия често се приема погрешно като първоначалото на медитацията. Но Индия не е единствения извор. Както е показано в началото на тази статия, медитацията е възникнала поотделно поне в Китай, Индия и Палестина преди наличието на написани исторически извори.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"cHGTS50xqo","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"lj6mmvyhyab","text":"Медитацията е вродена практика, естествен резултат от интроспекцията и затова няма едно място на произход. Вместо това, тя се открива навсякъде, както и когато човек насочи погледа си навътре.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"VJobnARHol","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"5z8y6yblqqt","text":"Кой е измислил медитацията?","type":"header","level":"h3","decorations":{}}},{"id":"tpbCw43XtV","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"vvvx2km4u4","text":"Истината е, че нито един човек или култура не са измислили медитацията, тя е естествен резултат от човешката интроспекция.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"_9lJPd08b9","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"c3746r0dz4","text":"Често срещано погрешно схващане е, че медитацията е измислена от Гаутама Буда. Самата будистка традиция описва, че Буда всъщност е бил обучаван от други на медитация, въпреки че я е намерил за недостатъчна и е разработил свой собствен подход.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"l3YyrKz0QY","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"qz2j0lzqij","text":"Друго погрешно схващане е, че медитацията е измислена от ранните индийски мъдреци и е записана в Упанишадите. Въпреки, че това е в основата на много съвременни практики, то не е напълно вярно. Можем да видим независими описания на медитацията в даоизма, юдаизма и суфизма - и това са само имената на най-известните религиозни практики.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"dc0z_xnUrq","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"nwe2fvay8nh","text":"Съвременна медитация","type":"header","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"2SGZhF8CGi","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"cylmtf2avw9","text":"В миналото хората, търсещи познание за себе си, са се отправяли на големи разстояния: раннохристиянските „отци пустинници“ са живели в пустините на Египет; индийските ученици са търсили гуру в планините. Християните и будистите се отделят от обществото в отдалечени манастири. В днешно време подобни практики вече не са необходими. Всеки сам може да опита медитация и да намери отговора в себе си.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"ipB0nuTF2x","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"reprgqg7ip","text":"През последното десетилетие се наблюдава поредното възраждане на медитацията в цялата съвременна западна култура. Голяма част от това възраждане са уж светски медитативни практики под знамето на осъзнатостта. Всъщност обаче осъзнатостта се корени в будизма, по-специално с акцент върху практиката „ānāpānasati“, осъзнатост на дишането. Някои форми на осъзнатост са представени по-светски от други, но всички се основават на тези техники. Осъзнатостта предлага подход за фокусиране и съсредоточаване, а в по-редки случаи и подход за наблюдаване на заобикалящия ви свят.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"GMjWO83hEv","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"89wrx1f680c","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"„The Conjunction“, CW 14, пар. 708., Карл Юнг","text":"„Ако древното изкуство на медитацията изобщо се практикува днес, то се практикува само в религиозни или философски кръгове, където темата се избира субективно от медитиращия или се предписва от инструктор, както е в „Игнатиевите упражнения“ или в някои теософски упражнения, развили се под индийско влияние. Тези методи са полезни единствено за повишаване на концентрацията и укрепване на съзнанието, но нямат никакво значение за синтеза на личността. Напротив, тяхната цел е да предпазят съзнанието от несъзнаваното и да го потиснат.“","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"Y7bPUqX91j","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"8nmsjv3pi8e","text":"За разлика от традиционния будизъм и други древни техники, майндфулнес е външно насочена практика, свързана с управлението на външното внимание на човека. На този уебсайт представяме една различна съвременна медитативна техника, основана на по-старите по-вътрешно фокусирани медитативни практики. Тя е подобна на медитацията описана по-горе от Карл Юнг, и на целите, които са описани в много медитативни практики в миналото - себепознание и вътрешно пробуждане.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"UUQRFi4zJR","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"gvfd1uqvwdi","text":"В живота има много повече от земния ум и първото докосване до реалността се открива с онази искра на божественото в състояние на възвишена тишина.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"5V2t8M6E43","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"63177qikyeu","text":"Сахаджа йога","type":"header","level":"h3","decorations":{}}},{"id":"kXYnKBOCeG","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"qdq3ojhupm","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"Лекция в Лонавала, Индия 1982","credit":"Шри Матаджи Нирмала Деви","text":"„Днес въпросите и отговорите бяха много хубави. Хареса ми начина, по който бяха зададени, по който бяха дадени отговори. Но най-добрият начин за изучаване на Сахаджа йога е практическата ѝ страна – също както в науката.“","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"center","style":"hero","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"FpJIwsuk8M","type":"media","data":{"id":"27dshgipu1t","poster":{},"items":[{"image":{"id":1236,"preview":"https://assets.wemeditate.com/uploads/media_file/file/1236/small_54b8265348.jpg?version="},"alt":"","caption":"","credit":""}],"mediaFiles":[1236],"youtube_id":"","type":"image","quantity":"single","position":"center","size":"narrow","decorations":{}}},{"id":"08Ad_KrT-2","type":"whitespace","data":{"id":"z7jphkxyf1a","size":"small","decorations":{}}},{"id":"UP8UjhhPvk","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"j3umt6pi4xq","text":"Медитациите представени на този уебсайт са модерни медитативни практики наречени Сахаджа йога, което се превежда като „Спонтанен съюз (връзка)“ или „Връзка без усилие“. Това е техника основана на опита, която изисква от вас първо да преживеете медитацията и след това да базирате разбирането си на този опит. Методът е разработен от Шри Матаджи Нирмала Деви през 1970 г. Той започва със Себереализация, след което човек развива това самопознание (познание за истинската ни същност) чрез медитация и различни поддържащи техники.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"CQdYwOgsAu","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"11y8oyskrkzh","text":"В уебсайта е предоставена допълнителна информация, но преди да продължите ви препоръчваме да:","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"YZJ4sYzDvx","type":"action","data":{"id":"de4zgacgcc","title":"","subtitle":"","text":"","action":"го преживеете","url":"/meditations/first-experience","list_id":"","type":"button","form":"signup","spacing":"spaced","decorations":{"leaves":true}}},{"id":"a1Ec4PxeBy","type":"catalog","data":{"id":"en4a7kjdhe","title":"Прочетете повече","items":["50"],"type":"articles","style":"image","decorations":{}}}],"version":"2.23.2","markupVersion":3,"mediaFiles":[]}

translations.name: History of Meditation
translations.content:
{"time":1675554569250,"blocks":[{"id":"Hqnr8FRCkK","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"dyp99lhalv","text":"The earliest recorded descriptions of meditation are found in India. Sacred Indian texts are the most often cited origin of meditation, but that is far from the full story. Indian texts are neither the only original source, nor are they even the only source from that time period. Meditative practices are found in cultures across the ancient world - from indigenous North America, to Greece, Mesopotamia and China.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"NoQko42yoc","type":"media","data":{"id":"3rpqjnthci3","poster":{},"items":[{"image":{"id":1233,"preview":"https://assets.wemeditate.com/uploads/media_file/file/1233/small_453310722b.jpg?version="},"alt":"","caption":"Illustration from \"Secret of the Golden Flower\" (8th century CE)","credit":""}],"mediaFiles":[1233],"youtube_id":"","type":"image","quantity":"single","position":"center","size":"narrow","decorations":{}}},{"id":"w6w3X9J2zz","type":"whitespace","data":{"id":"t7np434wb6g","size":"small","decorations":{}}},{"id":"sOcq_yLCvM","type":"list","data":{"id":"w4gmwosuoqo","items":[{"text":"Origins of meditation","level":"h2"},{"text":"What is meditation?","level":"h3"},{"text":"How long has meditation been around?","level":"h2"},{"text":"Ancient Meditation Practices","level":"h2"},{"text":"Ancient Meditation Techniques","level":"h3"},{"text":"Meditation Practices in Religion","level":"h2"},{"text":"Religions of Indian Origin","level":"h3"},{"text":"Jain Meditation","level":"h4"},{"text":"Hindu Meditation","level":"h4"},{"text":"Traditional / Theravada Buddhist Meditation","level":"h4"},{"text":"Zen / Chan Buddhist Meditation","level":"h4"},{"text":"Abrahamic Religions","level":"h3"},{"text":"Jewish Meditation","level":"h4"},{"text":"Christian Meditation","level":"h4"},{"text":"Islamic / Sufi Meditation","level":"h4"},{"text":"Religions of Chinese Origin","level":"h3"},{"text":"Daoist Meditation","level":"h4"},{"text":"Confucian Meditation","level":"h4"},{"text":"Western Meditation Practices","level":"h2"},{"text":"So where did meditation come from?","level":"h2"},{"text":"Who invented meditation?","level":"h3"},{"text":"Modern Meditation","level":"h2"},{"text":"Sahaja Yoga","level":"h3"}],"type":"contents"}},{"id":"uSlLVQ_LAI","type":"whitespace","data":{"id":"oszeu8d8dja","size":"small","decorations":{}}},{"id":"IstTv5VCYb","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"ju6gzayz99a","text":"Origins of meditation","type":"header","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"0LU83G5sPE","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"w8kr4276o4k","text":"Many of the most widely practiced techniques in modern day have their roots in India, including Zen, Mindfulness, various new age practices found in the West, and of course Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain meditation. However, once you look further, you will find practices worldwide with no obvious connection to that lineage: Jewish references to meditation in the Torah are as old as the Hindu references in the Upanishads; Daoism has certainly been influenced by Buddhism, but Daoist meditation predates the arrival of Buddhism in China; The writings of the Hellenic philosopher, Plotinus, have had a lasting influence on meditation practices in Europe and the Western Asia,","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"GBsCCj-Zb5","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"o53lf9d1f7p","text":"Then there are the practices that clearly predate recorded history: Judaism, Jainism, Buddhism, and of course Hinduism all have clear references to teachers of meditation in their earliest texts. These texts are often laying down an existing oral tradition rather than introducing a new practice.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"Tnjs35MzKK","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"ztrky7rzb09","text":"The exact origin of meditation cannot be defined, but its purposes are clear. It has existed before recorded history, and separately originated in many cultures across the globe. This article will demonstrate that despite these varied origins, meditation has a common core across cultures. Meditation at its essence is a practice of introspection and self-realisation. These practices have evolved across the world independently because introspection is a natural process in human life, and self-realisation is a natural evolution of that process.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"FbpVEjGcIh","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"w5u0iu9znfc","text":"What is meditation?","type":"header","level":"h3","decorations":{}}},{"id":"UfCncSImd9","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"zhatej5o9r","text":"Meditation is an experience, rather than an action - free from thought, but aware of one's surroundings. It's not an action to be done, but rather a state of being where one becomes connected. In this state you are conscious and aware, but momentarily thoughtless. Through practice one can develop this state, and grow the length of that thoughtless moment into a full state of meditation.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"l32vOLYtDq","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"2lez1whamd3","text":"Typical depictions of meditation will show a person sitting cross-legged, kneeling, or even standing on one leg. It's more difficult to depict what is going on inside. The inner experience is something which can only be obtained by being in meditation. Many techniques to achieve meditation involve postures, affirmations, or preparing your surroundings - but these activities themselves are not yet meditation. Put simply: Meditation is a state of thoughtless awareness.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"mu30C3GiVm","type":"action","data":{"id":"jqnjqpmcpq","title":"","subtitle":"","text":"","action":"Read more about meditation","url":"/articles/what-is-meditation","list_id":"","type":"button","form":"signup","spacing":"spaced","decorations":{}}},{"id":"yH2ZPx9BJx","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"he1wme4sbz","text":"How long has meditation been around?","type":"header","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"7Q2UOjssTY","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"kozli3stkhq","text":"There are many practices which are grouped under the term meditation. Amongst all those different practices, the earliest extensive descriptions are of dhyāna (ध्यान) in the Upanishad Vedas (Indian sacred texts). However the concept and practice of meditation existed in at least India and Palestine well before these first extensive recordings.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"Vsr9eVbPXB","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"cvj4uxlrjyt","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"Kaushitaki Upanishad 3.2, ~6th or 5th century BCE","text":"\"With mind, meditate (dhyāna) on me as being prana (life force)\"","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"WMUGGmO4Cq","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"ikkwl7f3xh","text":"The Torah (written ~6th century BCE, based on earlier oral traditions) describes Isaac as going to lasuach (לשוח) in a field - a word which is universally understood to describe a form of meditation. Judaism has used meditation for thousands of years, and those practices have filtered through to the Abrahamic religions that followed (Christianity and Islam).","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"JRDe83prU6","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"ija0a6pbnpe","title":"How old is meditation?","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"","text":"Meditation has been around since at least the 6th or 7th century BCE, where it is first mentioned in Hindu, Daoist, and Jewish sacred texts.","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"center","style":"hero","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"erVrr25HEa","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"cdaljhawrzd","text":"The three major Indian traditions - Jainism, Hinduism, and Buddhism - have clear references to meditation predating the Upanishads. Gautama Buddha - the founder of Buddhism - is described as having practiced meditation under two teachers. Jain tradition states the meditation has been a core practice, long before recorded history.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"5iR7_dlDRE","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"bqh68olu4ro","text":"In China, the earliest descriptions of meditation are from the Neiye (Inward training, ~4th century BCE) - a pivotal Daoist text. Neiye contains the oldest known descriptions of Chinese meditation and breath techniques.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"uhvfCInItb","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"6hd0ljsqpwn","text":"Looking towards the west, the greek philosopher Plotinus (3rd century CE) described henosis (ἕνωσις) - a union or oneness with what is fundamental in reality. He detailed several steps to this process, the second phase being that \"the intellect ... must ‘withdraw backwards’ and surrender itself to what lies behind it\" (Enneads III.8.9). His ideas have had an important impact on meditation traditions in Judaism, Gnosticism, and Islam, but were most notably adopted into Eastern Orthodox Christianity, where it is known as theoria (or contemplation) and theosis (unification with God).","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"pPuc2QQxn6","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"3su4tn375qd","text":"These early meditation practices have continued most commonly through the mystical traditions of various religions (where the primary goal is a direct experience of the divine / universe).","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"k6wQCq2DNx","type":"list","data":{"id":"m48nbao6bb","items":[{"text":"Indian traditions spread through Tibet and China, becoming Zen Buddhism in the east."},{"text":"Hinduism and Jainism continued to develop at home, as well as influence meditation in Sikhism."},{"text":"Hesychasm in Eastern Christianity and Hermetic Western Christianity is born of Jewish and Greek Influences."},{"text":"Sufism, the mystical branch of Islam, was influenced both by Judeo-Christian and Greek practices, as well as direct Indian influences in the Mughal-ruled India on Emperor Akbar."}],"type":"text","style":"unordered"}},{"id":"si9NJXbuGt","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"kndl0pl4ov","text":"Ancient Meditation Practices","type":"header","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"a56quUHwp5","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"b1pyll1nbd8","text":"According to ancient meditation practices, within each person lies a dormant energy, known variously as kundalini (India), pneuma (Greece), ki / chi (Japan / China), orenda (Iroquois), mana (Polynesia), and so on. Ancient meditation practices, especially those described in Indian scriptures focus on awakening this energy.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"av33lxgpwW","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"bb1mbhkdhss","text":"For thousands of years, ascetics (a person who gives up worldly life and possessions) would spend a lifetime in remote regions, such as the Himalayan mountains, seeking this awakening through prayer and penance.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"oPfn5PX2TU","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"er5ammkt0tl","text":"Ancient Meditation Techniques","type":"header","level":"h3","decorations":{}}},{"id":"jDLIeGcf5k","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"kem9kxiqnxd","text":"Yoga is now known as a common type of physical exercise. In truth, yoga stems from ancient techniques which Indian sages used to awaken the kundalini energy within them. The word yoga means \"union,\" as this was the goal of any yoga practitioner of that time. Physical postures, called āsana, are just one small part of these ancient techniques, which also include breathe control, austerity, ethical behaviour, mantras and more.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"0OmsrHud8g","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"rkantg7dxn","text":"Breath control is perhaps the most accessible and widely described ancient technique, as a first step towards thoughtlessness. However, breath control, mantras, and physical postures are external techniques. Meditation is an inward experience - as described in most ancient texts - these external approaches must be accompanied by self-study and introspection.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"gWO_Jl0qrD","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"2mr6gunceqg","text":"In addition to the dormant energy within us, there is also a subtle system encompassing that energy and various energy nodes (called chakras) within that system. Each chakra corresponds to a plexus of your nervous system, and ancient techniques hold that one can achieve the awakening of this energy through the management and balancing of one's chakras. You can learn more about this by exploring the chart of the subtle system, and reading about each chakra.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"wrgdtk0Uwj","type":"media","data":{"id":"4hqjlu20mh9","poster":{},"items":[{"image":{"id":1231,"preview":"https://assets.wemeditate.com/uploads/media_file/file/1231/small_184ed12cba.jpg?version="},"alt":"","caption":"Shri Krishna, known as the \"Lord of Yoga\" in Hindu practices.","credit":""}],"mediaFiles":[1231],"youtube_id":"","type":"image","quantity":"single","position":"right","size":"narrow","decorations":{}}},{"id":"0gdUjMWJvf","type":"whitespace","data":{"id":"grwnvcxtmku","size":"small","decorations":{}}},{"id":"t7Bw7DfdYt","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"wiqqm9rjk2r","text":"Meditation Practices in Religion","type":"header","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"utCw7P4Y5e","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"0eajxgh5i76j","text":"In this section, we'll give an overview of how meditation is described in each school of meditation across different religions.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"nK6E0pAI3q","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"pxgc0gibtn","text":"Throughout these descriptions, you will see a common theme of meditation being used as a tool towards self-realisation and union with the universe / divine / reality.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"5LO7Wxl2LW","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"jx9e0moo8gk","text":"Or, skip to Western Meditation Practices ⇒","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"8TDf9Q0YjX","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"2pmq0elcwb3","text":"Religions of Indian Origin","type":"header","level":"h3","decorations":{}}},{"id":"zxd_eWlp8d","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"4g6o5s8ifsn","text":"Jain Meditation","type":"header","level":"h4","decorations":{}}},{"id":"gmYjpYXxBC","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"e7fcwpl4b9f","text":"Known as sāmāyika (attaining equanimity).","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"XYbnz2ye8I","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"sglpei5g5s","text":"Jainism originates in the pre-Vedic period of India, perhaps India's oldest meditation tradition. Daily meditation is a key practice, taking the form of a 48 minute session, 1 - 3 times a day. Sāmāyika is described as the \"act of being conscious of the continual renewal of the universe in general and one's own renewal of the individual living being in particular, [as] the critical first step in the journey towards identification with one's true nature.\"","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"rDJgKANNvk","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"bnpip7933qr","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"From Purushartha Siddhyupaya, 95 ~10th century","text":"\"After renouncing all attachments and aversions, and adopting a sense of equanimity in all objects, one should practise, many times, periodic concentration (sāmāyika), the principal means to realize the true nature of the Self.\"","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"gh76D8t58-","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"pjg7msucnb","text":"Hindu Meditation","type":"header","level":"h4","decorations":{}}},{"id":"PyCDPZX16J","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"864s8ailm28","text":"Known as dhyāna (ध्यान, meditation).","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"dbz_WfeOth","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"1exkh1q27sbi","text":"The Upanishads, the Bhagavad Gita, and the Yoga Sutras are the primary sources for Hindu meditation. It has been further elaborated by countless Indian sages since then. In Hinduism, meditation is a key part of the process of yoga (union), where one comes to realise the atman (self or soul), their relation with other living beings, and the ultimate reality.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"CkXBEygAvV","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"vf93tijzyc","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"Bhagavad Gita 6.10, ~2nd century BCE. Translation by Juan Mascaro","text":"“Day after day, let the Yogi practice the harmony of soul: in a secret place, in deep solitude, master of his mind, hoping for nothing, desiring nothing.”","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"BDTjp8hYGN","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"beymcfmy98a","text":"Traditional / Theravada Buddhist Meditation","type":"header","level":"h4","decorations":{}}},{"id":"DqWqtrmI4k","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"48xroioua2e","text":"Known as dhyana (ध्यान, meditation) or jhāna (झान, meditation). ","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"-u9fT0Qh2D","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"05y0vimxmed4","text":"Buddhists practice meditation as a part of a path towards enlightenment and nirvana (liberation or salvation). This includes a wide variety of different techniques including breath-control, mindfulness, compassionate attention, and so on.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"56Y1sQzugr","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"cdba4rl7ben","text":"Traditional buddhist meditation generally revolves around the 4 rupa-jhānas (worldly meditations) as described in the Pāli Canon (sacred Buddhist texts, circa 29 BCE). Each of these being a sequential step towards the ultimate awakening. Briefly summarised, these stages are described as:","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"VdiaQuyERX","type":"list","data":{"id":"884868xegku","items":[{"text":"Separation from external sensations, while discursive thought continues."},{"text":"Inner tranquility, free from directed thought and evaluation."},{"text":"Equanimity, mindful, and alert; but sensing pleasure within the body."},{"text":"Pure equanimity and mindfulness, with neither pleasure nor pain."}],"type":"text","style":"ordered"}},{"id":"N6TvFLumK8","type":"media","data":{"id":"7fcca9oxmag","poster":{},"items":[{"image":{"id":1232,"preview":"https://assets.wemeditate.com/uploads/media_file/file/1232/small_8b1f61a8be.jpg?version="},"alt":"","caption":"Bodhidharma, the first Chinese patriarch of Chan Buddhism, seated in meditation.","credit":"Yoshitoshi, 1887"}],"mediaFiles":[1232],"youtube_id":"","type":"image","quantity":"single","position":"right","size":"narrow","decorations":{}}},{"id":"tRZJpXecsN","type":"whitespace","data":{"id":"wsd0lpm1rt","size":"small","decorations":{}}},{"id":"khLZ8XVuBo","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"ttk6eeh65uo","text":"Zen / Chan Buddhist Meditation","type":"header","level":"h4","decorations":{}}},{"id":"peM1blSH9N","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"077nl863z3qa","text":"Known as zazen (坐禅, seated meditation), kenshō (見性, seeing) and satori ( 悟り, comprehension).","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"noK_zG8NW4","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"udgli6y4xg9","text":"A widespread evolution of Buddhism practiced throughout east Asia. Chan Buddhism traveled from India, through China and then to Japan, Korea, Vietnam and elsewhere - where it is known under slight different regional names. The name itself is derived from dhyāna (ध्यान, meditation), reflecting this tradition's central emphasis on meditation.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"QBwr48qTbY","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"cc8q96v7rh8","text":"When Buddhism arrived in China, there was a significant cultural exchange with Daoism - a native Chinese religion, with its own meditation practices. This branch of Buddhism places a more clear emphasis on stilling or pacifying the mind, compared to traditional Buddhism. Here the central focus is on awakening one's Buddha-nature, which is said to be already present, subconsciously, in all sentient beings.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"VL3RdSZ2DE","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"vl5ogry8rfm","text":"In Japan (Zen Buddishm), this awakening is known as satori (悟り, comprehension), which is a deep experience of kenshō (見性, seeing). In this awakening one is said to see their own true nature, as well as the true Buddha-nature of all those around them. This awakening, through meditation, is the singular goal of Zen Buddhism.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"u4MPgktXWD","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"5dqmzaz2ngf","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"The Zen Teaching of Bodhidharma","text":"\"But people of the deepest understanding look within, distracted by nothing. Since a clear mind is the Buddha, they attain the understanding of a Buddha without using the mind.\"","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"aMAANKwrh7","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"upwgvkptt6i","text":"Abrahamic Religions","type":"header","level":"h3","decorations":{}}},{"id":"wwEsG3soVQ","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"4yx6lqeyziv","text":"Jewish Meditation","type":"header","level":"h4","decorations":{}}},{"id":"ifiXzfiXkE","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"9ur9jo94dan","text":"Known as hitbodedut (התבודדות, self-seclusion), lasauch (לשוח, meditation) and devekut (דבקות, cleaving to God). ","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"2cFB1aOPuO","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"8wycpri9y04","text":"Early Jewish sources - including the Hebrew Bible and the philosopher Maimonides - reference meditation, but provide no instruction on meditation techniques.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"8-scG0OA7k","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"adtt4emwti6","text":"The schools of Judaism are quite varied, and there is not a single widely accepted method of meditation. However, the main descriptions of meditation are given in Kabbalistic, Hasidic, and Mussar writings. These techniques often involve seclusion, mental visualisations and kavanot (mystical intentions).","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"S-Umoy5jTI","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"aqsbf7eutw","text":"Christian Meditation","type":"header","level":"h4","decorations":{}}},{"id":"RewYRufkPD","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"h7s2n54y56c","text":"Known as theosis (union with God) or simply meditation/contemplative prayer. ","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"iTpbGYTF-1","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"dxb7rbdqs5f","text":"Christianity as a religion is built on Judaism, and of course draws on those early Jewish meditation practices. The earliest mystical and meditative movement in Christianity was the Desert Fathers. These informal gatherings of Christian hermits lived in the deserts of Egypt and become the central origin of Christian monasticism and mysticism. The most notable continuation of that tradition was in Hesychasm, a movement of the Eastern Orthodox Church. The ultimate goal of hesychast meditation is theosis, a direct experience of the divine \"uncreated light,\" associated with the holy ghost.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"nGVSK4V3lZ","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"twihni7edym","text":"In Western Christianity, other meditation techniques were developed and described by Christian saints, especially the Catholic spanish mystics of the 16th and 17th century CE - such as Ignatius of Loyola, Teresa of Ávila, and Hildegard von Bingen.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"RpgpgyxSjG","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"2dhgp1nqbhj","text":"In both Western and Eastern Christianity, meditation is seen as one of three forms of prayer (alongside vocal prayer and contemplative prayer). Contemplative prayer itself, is not far from a form meditation either. It is described as seeking a direct awareness of the divine, and transcending the intellect.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"024RhNCiI7","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"m38nr442kx","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"Interior Castle, 1577 by Teresa of Ávila","text":"\"Just as we cannot stop the movement of the heavens, revolving as they do with such speed, so we cannot restrain our thought. [...] Yet the soul may perhaps be wholly united with Him in the Mansions very near His presence, while thought remains in the outskirts of the castle.\"","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"6R6t33bQFV","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"va5xdzxcfla","text":"Islamic / Sufi Meditation","type":"header","level":"h4","decorations":{}}},{"id":"TQ8RvocCiN","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"lak63sregj","text":"Known as murāqabah (مراقبة, to observe). ","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"SF2YRqhKhZ","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"6nx24jencwf","text":"Several Islamic meditative practices exist (eg. salah and dhikr), but the most developed form of meditation in Islam, is the murāqabah performed by Sufi mystics. Islam is a part of the same Abrahamic tradition as Christianity and Judaism, recognising many of the same prophets and holy texts, and so Islam has inherited some of those influences, as well as direct influences from India and West Asia.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"1gEktggieg","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"034s03dfd9i9","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"By Rumi a Sufi poet","text":"“Your task is not to seek for love, but merely to seek and find all the barriers within yourself that you have built against it.”","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"Z-8GPhBBh5","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"k9mt6rtxhw","text":"In Sufism, murāqabah is described as having several stages. As we've seen with other practices, the final stage here is to achieve a state of thoughtless awareness. There are three stages of murāqabah:","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"IaXxlcMxQb","type":"list","data":{"id":"1le6vaxwqo3","items":[{"text":"Somnolence - a state between sleep and waking, while often slipping into a sleep state."},{"text":"Idrāk - with practice, the sleepiness of meditation decreases. The conscious mind is aware and able to receive spiritual knowledge from the subconscious."},{"text":"Wurūd - awareness is maintained with somnolence at a minimum. The person becomes sublimated in the experience, no longer an outsider."}],"type":"text","style":"ordered"}},{"id":"L21wvkUXQ4","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"8loqdxswb5p","text":"Religions of Chinese Origin","type":"header","level":"h3","decorations":{}}},{"id":"tSSKkX3ziU","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"uesluyerqkm","text":"Daoist Meditation","type":"header","level":"h4","decorations":{}}},{"id":"9TtsZUPLWV","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"zgdme02duz","text":"Known as xiu dao (修道, practicing the way) and zuowang (坐忘, sitting forgetting). ","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"So4pqRDIKk","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"2jjphjtd1t6","text":"Meditation is a central practice in Daoism. It is described in almost every significant Daoist text - Zhuangzi, Dao de Jing, Neiye, and others. In this meditation, one seeks a loss of self, and a complete immersion in the universe. Frequently texts discuss discarding one's external senses and reasoning powers in order to enter a state of thoughtlessness.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"7ljEFSTTYH","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"9r79gqocy6s","text":"There are several common phrases used to describe Daoist meditation that give a sense of its purpose and character, such as \"guarding the one\" (守一), \"fasting the heartmind\" (心齋), and \"embracing simplicity\" (抱朴).","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"1EYoJ-VU_5","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"uvehaycf5w","text":"The word Dao itself - often translated as \"Way\" or \"Path\" - is described as underlying flow or pattern of the universe, its natural order. Through Daoist meditation, one seeks to become one with this natural order.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"tjIoJc3axW","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"6wff75mhrq3","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"Zhuangzi, translation by James Legge","text":"\"My connection with the body and its parts is dissolved; my perceptive organs are discarded. Thus leaving my material form, and bidding farewell to my knowledge, I am become one with the Great Pervader. This I call sitting and forgetting all things.\"","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"q6svv8DXLu","type":"media","data":{"id":"cn8i3em2esw","poster":{},"items":[{"image":{"id":1230,"preview":"https://assets.wemeditate.com/uploads/media_file/file/1230/small_c91645ac83.jpg?version="},"alt":"","caption":"Quietly Listening to Wind in the Pines","credit":"Ma Lin, 13th Century"}],"mediaFiles":[1230],"youtube_id":"","type":"image","quantity":"single","position":"right","size":"narrow","decorations":{}}},{"id":"x6FF6lcHOE","type":"whitespace","data":{"id":"ylju9dpw5jr","size":"small","decorations":{}}},{"id":"_GFJ-4XYdD","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"bpqwub45qrd","text":"Confucian Meditation","type":"header","level":"h4","decorations":{}}},{"id":"ztBy93DkUV","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"77jqpl3b2rm","text":"Known as jing zuo (靜坐, quiet sitting).","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"wPAhw3HVuS","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"iwb3mva8i7n","text":"Meditation was not a major part of Confucianism until Buddhism and Daoism started to have a major influence in Chinese culture. Around the 11th century, Confucianism was reinterpreted in the context of Buddhist and Daoist thought. This is usually called Neo-Confucianism. As a result, Confucian meditation is often described in contrast to Buddhist meditation. Like other forms of meditation, the ultimate goal is the full realisation of one's self, but there are two competing schools of thought - the Rational and Idealistic school.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"zhEN84msXY","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"y6jj4hr90v","text":"Neo-Confucian scholars described their meditation - jing zuo - as \"oriented to this world and aimed at perfecting one's self, whereas Buddhist and Daoist meditation focused on forgetting the world and abandoning one's self.\" In the rational school, action and knowledge, and an active investigation of the world are considered key.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"4YyKl3-mlb","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"jxaum8exm1o","text":"However, in the Idealistic school of thought, we can find a familiar theme. Wang Yangming, an influential figure in this school, believed that only way to enlightenment was reflection on an inner principle, which exists in everyone. In the Idealistic school, only self-examination and inward study are needed to achieve enlightenment.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"OQSAbaJ5XS","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"8yfkg05yt0e","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"Instructions for Practical Living and Other Neo-Confucian Writings (傳習錄), Wang Yangming","text":"\"Nothing exists outside our minds, no supreme principle exists outside our hearts.\"","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"DdDr7Iwt-Q","type":"media","data":{"id":"n3uyi06ev","poster":{},"items":[{"image":{"id":1229,"preview":"https://assets.wemeditate.com/uploads/media_file/file/1229/small_002d22d4ff.jpg?version="},"alt":"Handwriting of Wang Yangming","caption":"Writings of Wang Yangming, an influential figure in Confucian meditation ","credit":""}],"mediaFiles":[1229],"youtube_id":"","type":"image","quantity":"single","position":"center","size":"wide","decorations":{}}},{"id":"eVYMMkj2-4","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"zaosj9gsoor","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"Translation by David Hinton","credit":"The Zhuangzi, Chapter 4","text":"Replied Confucius, \"So many decrees! You lay down laws, but you don't think things through. Yes, it's true you'd stop his wrath. But that's all you'd stop. How would you get him to change? You're still making the mind a teacher.\"
\"Then I'm all out of ideas,\" said Yen Hui finally. \"May I ask what your strategy would be?\"
\"Fasting,\" replied Confucius. \"Let me explain something to you. Using your mind to do things - isn't that too easy? And the easy way rarely accords with bright heaven.\"
\"My house is poor,\" said Yen Hui. \"It's been months since I've tasted wine or meat. Isn't that considered fasting?\"
\"That's the fasting of Ceremony and Ritual,\" replied Confucius. \"Not the mind's fast.\"
\"May I ask about the mind's fast?\"\"Center your attention,\" began Confucius. \"Stop listening with your ears and listen with your mind. Then stop listening with your mind and listen with your primal spirit. Hearing is limited to the ear. Mind is limited to tallying things up. But the primal spirit is empty: it is simply that which awaits things. Way is emptiness merged, and emptiness is the mind's fast.\"","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"6Qcf-pxIjj","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"dqp8762vdkw","text":"Western Meditation Practices","type":"header","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"43_Jnkc8dM","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"f5ylu7dfcq8","text":"Meditation in the West is an ongoing and evolving practice, influenced heavily by Eastern traditions. Few meditative practices have survived in organised European religion and so much of the renewal of Western meditation has been fuelled by the study of eastern practices, as well as the migration of eastern mystics - particularly from India and China - to the West.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"WCMurJ1SrN","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"5poh9pmg08i","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"Walden, 1854 by Henry David Thoreau","text":"\"In the morning I bathe my intellect in the stupendous and cosmogonal philosophy of the Bhagavat Geeta, since whose composition years of the gods have elapsed, and in comparison with which our modern world and its literature seem puny and trivial; and I doubt if that philosophy is not to be referred to a previous state of existence, so remote is its sublimity from our conceptions.\"","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"zKh3Ik48Pn","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"5xn4oy22x1s","text":"The eastern and western worlds have not developed in isolation from each other. Europeans have studied the eastern culture since as far back as ancient Greece - where Greco-Buddhist societies formed in the eastern parts of Alexander the Great's empire. In 2nd millennium European scholars were shocked to discover the strong similarities between Latin and Sanskrit (the root languages of Europe and India respectively). The great transcendentalist thinkers of earlier American culture - Ralph Waldo Emerson, Henry David Thoreau, and others - delved deeply into the study of Indian sacred texts.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"h-7jwTKbUn","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"54u9db7kcuq","text":"Eastern influences are now virtually inseparable from the Western meditation. In the mid to late 20th century the American counter-culture movement and the migration of religious figures from communism in East Asia drove an explosion of interest in Eastern meditation practices in the West. Western meditation has very clear ties to eastern practices, but has also evolved to incorporate western outlooks. Carl Jung - an influential 20th century psychologist - gives his philosophy of meditation, a good example of a philosophy of drawing from eastern influence and adapted in the West.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"xGJaM0QU_C","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"9ecgdp2qb5","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"The Conjunction, CW 14, par. 709. by Carl Jung","text":"\"In general, meditation and contemplation have a bad reputation in the West. They are regarded as a particularly reprehensible form of idleness or as pathological narcissism. No one has time for self-knowledge or believes that it could serve any sensible purpose. Also, one knows in advance that it is not worth the trouble to know oneself, for any fool can know what he is. We believe exclusively in doing and do not ask about the doer, who is judged only by achievements that have collective value. The general public seems to have taken cognizance of the existence of the unconscious psyche more than the so-called experts, but still nobody has drawn any conclusions from the fact that Western man confronts himself as a stranger and that self-knowledge is one of the most difficult and exacting of the arts.\"","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"Bh8BkPI9IZ","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"z821j3hbrq","text":"Carl Jung, equated meditation in his words with \"coming to terms with the unconscious.\" It was a tool for real self-understanding, and in that sense he distanced it from religious meditation practices, that by his time had often become ritualistic or outward looking.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"-zUWREnEkI","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"dr98xwooosb","text":"So where did meditation come from?","type":"header","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"rshqAkUiZ3","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"7dsr0k2ildp","text":"The best tracked lineage of meditation originated in India, and then spread east to China with Buddhism - particularly becoming the Zen Buddhist tradition. Greek scholars and American transcendentalists studied this lineage. It has influenced Sufism through the Islamic rule of India. The most common modern practices have strong roots to this lineage, and so India is often mistaken for the source of meditation. But India is not the sole origin. As shown at the beginning of this article, meditation originated separately in at least China, India, and Palestine before recorded history.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"cHGTS50xqo","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"lj6mmvyhyab","text":"Meditation is an innate practice, the natural result of introspection, and so it has no single point of origin Instead it is found wherever and whenever one sets their sight within.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"VJobnARHol","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"5z8y6yblqqt","text":"Who invented meditation?","type":"header","level":"h3","decorations":{}}},{"id":"tpbCw43XtV","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"vvvx2km4u4","text":"The truth is that no single person or culture invented meditation, it is a natural result of human introspection.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"_9lJPd08b9","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"c3746r0dz4","text":"A common misconception is that meditation was invented by Gautama Buddha. Buddhist tradition itself describes that Buddha in fact was taught meditation by others, although he found it lacking and developed his own approach.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"l3YyrKz0QY","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"qz2j0lzqij","text":"Another misconception is that meditation was invented by early Indian sages and recorded in the Upanishads. While this is the root of many modern practices, it is not universally true. We can see independent depictions of meditation in Daoism, Judaism, and Sufism - and that is only to name the most well known religious practices.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"dc0z_xnUrq","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"nwe2fvay8nh","text":"Modern Meditation","type":"header","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"2SGZhF8CGi","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"cylmtf2avw9","text":"Historically those seeking knowledge of themselves would go to great lengths: the early christian Desert Fathers lived in the deserts of Egypt; Indian disciples sought gurus in the mountains. Christian and Buddhist removed themselves from society in remote monasteries. In the modern day, such practices are no longer necessary. Everyone can try meditation for themselves and find the answer within themselves.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"ipB0nuTF2x","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"reprgqg7ip","text":"In the recent decade there has been another resurgence of meditation throughout modern Western culture. Much of this resurgence are, supposedly secular, meditation practices under the banner of mindfulness. However mindfulness is in fact rooted in Buddhism, specifically with an emphasis on the practice of ānāpānasati, mindfulness of breathing. Some mindfulness is presented more secularly than others, but all draw on these techniques. Mindfulness offers an approach to focus and concentration, and in more rare circumstances an approach to being a witness of world around you.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"GMjWO83hEv","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"89wrx1f680c","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"The Conjunction, CW 14, par. 708. by Carl Jung","text":"\"If the ancient art of meditation is practised at all today, it is practised only in religious or philosophical circles, where a theme is subjectively chosen by the meditant or prescribed by an instructor, as in the Ignatian Exercitia or in certain theosophical exercises that developed under Indian influence. These methods are of value only for increasing concentration and consolidating consciousness, but have no significance as regards affecting a synthesis of the personality. On the contrary, their purpose is to shield consciousness from the unconscious and to suppress it.\"","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"Y7bPUqX91j","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"8nmsjv3pi8e","text":"In contrast to traditional Buddhism and other ancient techniques, Mindfulness is an externally focused practice, concerned managing one's external attentions. On this website we present a different modern meditation technique based on the older more internally-focused meditative practices. This is similar to the meditation described above by Carl Jung and the goals described in many historical meditation practices - self-knowledge and inner awakening.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"UUQRFi4zJR","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"gvfd1uqvwdi","text":"There is much more to life, than the mundane mind, and that first touch of reality is found with that spark of the divine in a state of sublime silence.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"5V2t8M6E43","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"63177qikyeu","text":"Sahaja Yoga","type":"header","level":"h3","decorations":{}}},{"id":"kXYnKBOCeG","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"qdq3ojhupm","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"Lecture at Lonavala, India 1982","credit":"Shri Mataji Nirmala Devi","text":"\"Now questions and answers were very good. I liked the way they were asked, answers were given. But the best way to learn Sahaj yoga is practical side of it — just like science.\"","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"center","style":"hero","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"FpJIwsuk8M","type":"media","data":{"id":"27dshgipu1t","poster":{},"items":[{"image":{"id":1236,"preview":"https://assets.wemeditate.com/uploads/media_file/file/1236/small_54b8265348.jpg?version="},"alt":"","caption":"","credit":""}],"mediaFiles":[1236],"youtube_id":"","type":"image","quantity":"single","position":"center","size":"narrow","decorations":{}}},{"id":"08Ad_KrT-2","type":"whitespace","data":{"id":"z7jphkxyf1a","size":"small","decorations":{}}},{"id":"UP8UjhhPvk","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"j3umt6pi4xq","text":"The meditations presented on this website are a modern meditation practice called Sahaja Yoga, meaning \"Spontaneous Union,\". This is an experience-based technique which asks you to experience meditation first and then base your understanding on that experience. This method was developed by Shri Mataji Nirmala Devi in 1970. It begins with self-realisation and then one develops that self-knowledge through meditation and various supporting techniques.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"S-DJdUOTXn","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"7uo7tolcam2","text":"Information is provided throughout this website, but before reading further, we encourage you to:","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"YZJ4sYzDvx","type":"action","data":{"id":"de4zgacgcc","title":"","subtitle":"","text":"","action":"Experience it yourself","url":"/meditations/first-experience","list_id":"","type":"button","form":"signup","spacing":"spaced","decorations":{"leaves":true}}},{"id":"a1Ec4PxeBy","type":"catalog","data":{"id":"en4a7kjdhe","title":"Further reading","items":["50"],"type":"articles","style":"image","decorations":{}}}],"version":"2.23.2","markupVersion":3,"mediaFiles":[]}

translations.name: Istoria Meditației
translations.content: {"time":1755096122335,"blocks":[{"id":"Hqnr8FRCkK","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"dyp99lhalv","text":"Primele izvoare istorice cu descrieri ale meditației se găsesc în India. În ceea ce privește originea meditației, textele sacre indiene sunt cel mai des evocate, dar aceasta nu este nici pe departe întreaga poveste. Textele indiene nu sunt singura sursă originară, nici măcar nu sunt singura sursă din acea perioadă istorică. IV","text":"- Atât de multe decrete, a spus Confucius. Inventați noi legi, dar nu gândiți lucrurile în profunzime. Da, este adevărat că i-ați potoli mânia. Dar acesta este singurul lucru pe care l-ați rezolva. Cum vreți să îl schimbați astfel? În continuare faceți din mintea voastră stăpân. - Atunci sunt complet dezarmat. Nu mai am alte idei, a spus în sfârșit Yen Hui. Îmi permiți să te întreb care ar fi strategia ta? - Postul, a răspuns Confucius. Permite-mi să îți explic. A-ți folosi mintea pentru a acționa – nu este oare cam prea comun? Și calea urmată de toți rareori duce spre rai. - Casa mea este săracă, a spus Yen Hui. Au trecut luni bune de când am gustat vin sau carne. Asta nu se consideră post? - Acesta este postul ritual, zise Confucius. Nu este postul minții.- Ce este postul minții, dacă îmi este permisă întrebarea? -Oprește-te din a asculta cu urechile și ascultă cu mintea. Apoi oprește-te din a asculta cu mintea și ascultă cu spiritul. Auzul este limitat la urechi, mintea este limitată la a căuta înțelesuri. Dar spiritul este infinit – este ceea ce stă mereu și așteaptă. Calea este revelată liniștii interioare, iar liniștea interioară este postul minții.","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"6Qcf-pxIjj","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"dqp8762vdkw","text":"Practici de meditație occidentale","type":"header","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"43_Jnkc8dM","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"f5ylu7dfcq8","text":"În occident, evoluția meditației este un proces în curs de derulare, influențat puternic de tradițiile răsăritene. Puține practici de meditație au supraviețuit în religiile europene organizate și multe cunoștințe și tehnici occidentale au fost împrumutate și preluate din tradițiile orientale, atât datorită interesului și studiului unor grupuri mici de persoane sau unor căutători individuali, cât și prin migrația misticilor din Orient – mai ales din India și China – spre Occident.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"WCMurJ1SrN","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"5poh9pmg08i","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"Walden (1854) de Henry David Thoreau","text":"Dimineața îmi scald intelectul în impresionanta și cosmogonica filosofie a Bhagavat Gita, de la a cărei compunere ani divini au trecut și în comparație cu care lumea noastră modernă și literatura ei par fade și triviale; și probabil nu greșesc când spun că acea filosofie vorbește despre o stare de existență precedentă, atât de departe în gingășia ei față de conceptele moderne.","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"kESl78O_M8","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"f92vn74d4vm","text":"Lumile orientală și occidentală nu au evoluat independent. Europenii au studiat culturile orientale încă din vremea Greciei antice – unde societăți greco-budiste s-au organizat în partea de est a imperiului lui Alexandru cel Mare. În mileniul al doilea, savanții europeni au fost șocați să descopere asemănările dintre limba latină și limba sanscrită. Marii gânditori transcendentali ai culturii americane timpurii – Ralph Waldo Emerson, Henry David Thoreau și alții – au aprofundat prin studiu textele sacre indiene.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"L0OefxBhRp","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"ktkjhgkqxb","text":"Influențele orientale sunt acum practic inseparabile de meditația occidentală. La mijlocul și spre sfârșitul secolului al XX-lea, mișcarea contraculturii americane din acea perioadă și migrarea unor personalități ecleziastice din blocul comunist spre Asia de est au condus la o creștere semnificativă a interesului occidentalilor față de meditație. Astfel, practicile de meditație din vest au rădăcini orientale, dar încorporează și viziuni și concepte autohtone. Carl Jung – un influent psiholog al secolului XX – are o filosofie proprie în legătură cu meditația, un foarte bun exemplu al modului în care se împletesc stilul occidental cu practicile provenite din orient.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"xGJaM0QU_C","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"9ecgdp2qb5","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"Carl Jung","text":"În general, meditația și contemplația au o reputație proastă în West. Sunt văzute ca forme indezirabile de trândăvie sau narcisism patologic. Nimeni nu are timp pentru cunoaștere de sine și nimeni nu consideră că aceste practici ar putea avea un scop rațional. Aici oamenii știu că nu se merită să încerci să te cunoști pe tine însuți, pentru că până și ultimul om știe despre sine cine este. Credem exclusiv în a face și nu punem întrebări legate de subiectul care acționează, care este judecat numai după reușitele ce au valoare în ochii majorității. Publicul general pare să fie mai conștient de existența un psihic colectiv inconștient decât așa numiții experți, dar încă nimeni nu a recunoscut oficial faptul că omul occidental se vede pe el însuși ca pe un străin și că, de fapt, cunoașterea de sine este cea mai dificilă și cea mai riguroasă artă.","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"Bh8BkPI9IZ","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"z821j3hbrq","text":"Carl Jung a echivalat cuvântul meditație cu „a fi în contact cu inconștientul" și a considerat că reprezintă o unealtă reală pentru înțelegerea de sine, și în acest sens a diferențiat-o de practicile de meditație religioase, care în acea perioadă ajunseseră deja mai degrabă ritualistice și orientate spre exterior.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"-zUWREnEkI","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"dr98xwooosb","text":"Deci de unde provine meditația?","type":"header","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"U81q-KGYdl","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"w5bgstwb4q","text":"Cea mai clară descendență își are originea în India și răspândirea ulterioară spre est, în China. Savanții greci și americanii transcendentaliști au studiat această descendență. A influențat sufismul prin dominația islamică în India. Cele mai întâlnite practici moderne au rădăcini profunde pe această linie. Ca urmare, la o analiză lipsită de rigoare, India poate fi considerată sursa meditației. Dar, în realitate, nu este singura. După cum am văzut la începutul articolului, meditația are origini independente cel puțin în India, China și Palestina, dinainte de apariția surselor scrise.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"grb3NKlzpx","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"08w8huuriohr","text":"Meditația este o practică înnăscută, rezultatul firesc al introspecției, prin urmare nu are o origine punctiformă, ci ne putem imagina că își are originea cu fiecare persoană din vechime care și-a îndreptat atenția spre interior.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"VJobnARHol","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"5z8y6yblqqt","text":"Cine a inventat meditația?","type":"header","level":"h3","decorations":{}}},{"id":"Jt76O8vRZP","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"js81saxr1n","text":"Adevărul este că nu a existat vreo persoană sau cultură care să fi inventat meditația, aceasta fiind un rezultat firesc al introspecției.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"3h4v5qVT-Z","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"06les9w1vzbu","text":"O idee greșită frecvent întâlnită este că a fost inventată de Gautama Siddartha. Tradiția budistă însăși vorbește despre faptul că Buddha a fost instruit să mediteze de către alte persoane, chiar dacă ulterior a considerat aceste învățături insuficiente și a ajuns la Adevăr pe cale individuală.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"ZHJhFeDJf5","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"zrl4tvq64u","text":"O altă idee greșită este că meditația a fost inventată de vechii înțelepți indieni și înregistrată grafic pentru prima dată în Upanișade. Deși aceasta este rădăcina multor practici moderne, afirmația nu este adevărată. Putem vedea descrieri independente în daoism, iudaism și sufism – ca să numim doar câteva dintre cele mai cunoscute practici religioase.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"dc0z_xnUrq","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"nwe2fvay8nh","text":"Meditația modernă","type":"header","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"7ZTm9Y6huB","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"o2uj7fmpvlj","text":"Privind în trecut, observăm că aproape toți căutătorii adevărului au călătorit în locuri îndepărtate pentru a găsi ceea ce căutau: Părinții Deșertului au trăit în deșertul Egiptului, discipolii indieni își căutau un guru în munți. Creștinii și budiștii se retrăgeau din societate ca să trăiască în mănăstiri izolate. În zilele noastre, asemenea practici nu mai sunt necesare. Cu toții putem încerca să medităm de unii singuri și putem găsi răspunsuri la întrebările pe care le avem.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"Nqq3YsHUbf","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"zvdiudi2tkj","text":"În ultimele două decenii a existat o „renaștere” a meditației în cultura occidentală modernă. În mare parte, ea se datorează popularizării a ceea ce se numește mindfulness. Totuși, mindfulness își are rădăcinile în budism, în special cu accent pe practici ānāpānasati, tehnici de respirație conștientă. Mindfulness oferă o alternativă pentru îmbunătățirea atenției și, în cazuri mai rare, o încercare de a permite practicantului să devină martorul lumii din exteriorul său.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"GMjWO83hEv","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"89wrx1f680c","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"","credit":"Carl Jung","text":"Dacă vechea artă a meditației mai este astăzi practicată în vreun fel, asta se întâmplă în cercuri religioase și filosofice restrânse, unde se alege la întâmplare o temă de către practicant sau de către un instructor, ca în Exercitia Spiritualia a lui Ignațiu de Loyola sau în anumite exerciții teosofice dezvoltate sub influență indiană. Aceste metode sunt utile numai pentru a îmbunătăți concentrarea și a consolida conștiința, dar sunt insignifiante în ceea ce privește sinteza personalității. Din contră, scopul lor este să izoleze conștientul de inconștient și să-l suprime.","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"left","style":"simple","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"2bHPB2lMTO","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"bd69pc76ar","text":"Spre deosebire de budismul tradițional și de alte tehnici antice, mindfulness este o practică orientată spre exterior, interesată să gestioneze modul în care subiectul privește lumea din jurul său. Pe aceste site, ne propunem să prezentăm o metodă de meditație modernă diferită, bazată mai degrabă pe practicile străvechi, orientate spre sinele interior. Această metodă seamănă cu meditația descrisă de Carl Jung și are ca scop ceea ce propuneau multe dintre practicile din vechime – cunoașterea de sine și trezirea interioară.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"0_Tsvbygy7","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"3hza47uaij4","text":"Viața este mult mai mult decât gândurile și grijile de toate zilele, iar trezirea esenței divine din om și întreținerea ei ulterioară pot schimba atât de mult din ceea ce noi numeam anterior realitate.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"5V2t8M6E43","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"63177qikyeu","text":"Sahaja Yoga","type":"header","level":"h3","decorations":{}}},{"id":"kXYnKBOCeG","type":"textbox","data":{"id":"qdq3ojhupm","title":"","subtitle":"","caption":"Conferință din Lonavala, India (1982)","credit":"Shri Mataji Nirmala Devi","text":"Întrebările și răspunsurile au fost foarte bune. Mi-a plăcut modul în care au fost formulate. Dar cea mai bună cale de a învăța Sahaja Yoga este latura ei practică – exact ca în știință.","action":"","url":"","mediaFiles":[],"type":"text","alignment":"center","style":"hero","spacing":"overlap","background":"white","color":"light","position":"left","decorations":{}}},{"id":"FpJIwsuk8M","type":"media","data":{"id":"27dshgipu1t","poster":{},"items":[{"image":{"id":1236,"preview":"https://assets.wemeditate.com/uploads/media_file/file/1236/small_54b8265348.jpg?version="},"alt":"","caption":"","credit":""}],"mediaFiles":[1236],"youtube_id":"","type":"image","quantity":"single","position":"center","size":"narrow","decorations":{}}},{"id":"08Ad_KrT-2","type":"whitespace","data":{"id":"z7jphkxyf1a","size":"small","decorations":{}}},{"id":"0KxNiWnLJA","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"6c8y4ilywxl","text":"Meditația prezentată pe acest site este o metodă modernă, numită Sahaja Yoga (unire spontană). Este o metodă practică care presupune să experimentezi întâi meditația, pentru ca ulterior să îți stabilizezi înțelegerea bazându-te pe experiența dobândită. A fost dezvoltată de Shri Mataji Nirmala Devi începând cu anul 1970. Începe cu Realizarea Sinelui, pentru ca ulterior practicantul să își dezvolte cunoașterea de sine prin meditație zilnică și mai multe tehnici ajutătoare.","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"fhfF4ik2WM","type":"paragraph","data":{"id":"gy88rbij64","text":"Mai multe informații îți stau la dispoziție pe acest site, dar înainte să continui să citești, te încurajăm să:","type":"text","level":"h2","decorations":{}}},{"id":"YZJ4sYzDvx","type":"action","data":{"id":"de4zgacgcc","title":"","subtitle":"","text":"","action":"Experimentezi tu însuți!","url":"/meditations/first-experience","list_id":"","type":"button","form":"signup","spacing":"spaced","decorations":{"leaves":true}}},{"id":"a1Ec4PxeBy","type":"catalog","data":{"id":"en4a7kjdhe","title":"Further reading","items":["50"],"type":"articles","style":"image","decorations":{}}}],"version":"2.23.2","markupVersion":3,"mediaFiles":[]}
